topics.title: Control how agents are shared
topics.summary: You can control and limit how agents are shared in your tenant by applying the Editor and Viewer permission assignments to individuals who need to access Copilot Studio, and then configuring the permissions for who can share with whom.

topics.summary: This article explains how to capture agent-level telemetry data from your Copilot Studio agent powered by the standard harness for use in Azure Application Insights.

topics.title: Use Power Platform connectors as tools in Copilot Studio agents
topics.summary: Connectors from Microsoft Power Platform act as proxies or "wrappers" around APIs. By using connectors, you can connect your accounts and use prebuilt tools and triggers to build your apps and work…

topics.title: Use agent flows with your agent
topics.summary: You can extend the capabilities of your agent by adding agent flows as tools. Agent flows are low-code automations that you build in Copilot Studio or Power Automate. When you add an agent flow as a tool, the agent's orchestrator can call the flow at runtime to retrieve data or perform actions on behalf of the user.

topics.title: Orchestrate agent behavior with generative AI
topics.summary: Agents powered by the standard harness can use either generative or classic orchestration. By default, new agents use generative orchestration. topics.title: Hand off to a live agent
topics.summary: By using Copilot Studio, you can configure your agent to hand off conversations to live agents seamlessly and contextually.

topics.title: Use a classic chatbot as an Azure Bot Service skill in an Azure Bot Service bot
topics.summary: This article applies to classic chatbots only. This feature isn't available for Copilot Studio agents powered by the standard or Microsoft Copilot harness.

topics.summary: This article includes information about Azure Bot Service skills , a code-based way to extend the capabilities of an agent in the standard harness. These skills shouldn't be confused with agentic skills in the Microsoft Copilot harness. Learn more about how to use agentic skills in Skills overview for agents.

topics.title: Extend your agent with Model Context Protocol
topics.summary: You can extend your agent with tools by using Model Context Protocol (MCP).

topics.title: Speed up agent flow execution with express mode (preview)
topics.summary: By default, an agent or app initiates an agent flow that fails if it takes longer than two minutes to respond to the calling agent or app. This failure affects the functionality and usability of the agent or app that calls the flow.

topics.title: Agent usage estimator
topics.summary: The Microsoft agent usage estimator is a transparent, client-facing tool that helps organizations forecast their monthly Copilot credit consumption across multiple AI agents in Microsoft Dynamics 365 and Copilot Studio.

topics.title: Add a Copilot Studio agent as a connected agent (Microsoft Copilot)
topics.summary: Use connected agents to let your primary agent delegate specific tasks to specialized agents. This article shows you how to add another published Copilot Studio agent as a connected agent and verify that delegation works as expected.

topics.title: Add a connected agent (Customer Conversation) (preview)
topics.summary: Use connected agents to let your primary agent delegate a request to an independent agent hosted in Microsoft Foundry. Unlike a sub-agent, a connected agent keeps its own configuration and lifecycle management, separate from your primary agent.

topics.title: Add a Foundry agent as a connected agent (Microsoft Copilot)
topics.summary: Use connected agents to let your primary agent delegate specific tasks to specialized agents. This article shows you how to connect an existing Microsoft Foundry agent so your primary agent can hand tasks off to it.

topics.title: Add a Microsoft 365 Agents SDK agent as a connected agent (Microsoft Copilot)
topics.summary: Use connected agents to let your primary agent delegate specific tasks to specialized agents. This article shows you how to connect an agent built with the Microsoft 365 Agents SDK, so your primary agent can hand tasks off to it.

topics.title: Add an Agent2Agent (A2A) agent as a connected agent (Microsoft Copilot)
topics.summary: Use connected agents to let your primary agent delegate specific tasks to specialized agents. This article shows you how to connect a remote agent that's available over the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol, so your primary agent can hand tasks off to it.

topics.title: Add a tool to an agent (Microsoft Copilot)
topics.summary: You can add tools to your agent from the Build tab. Tools let your agent perform actions, connect to external services, and retrieve real-time data during conversations.

topics.title: Add a tool to an agent (Customer Conversation) (preview)
topics.summary: You can add tools to your agent from the Build tab. Tools let your agent perform actions, connect to external services, and retrieve real-time data during conversations.

topics.title: Work IQ in Copilot Studio (Microsoft Copilot)
topics.summary: Work IQ is generally available in Microsoft Copilot Studio and is added by default to every new agent that uses the Microsoft Copilot harness. All available workloads are selected by default. You can narrow the selection to give your agent the work context it needs for your scenario. Some workloads, such as Business a…

topics.title: Create a test set for an agent (preview)
topics.summary: A test set is a collection of conversations you use to evaluate your agent's performance. Each conversation represents a scenario you want your agent to handle.

topics.title: Evaluate an agent (Customer Conversation) (preview)
topics.summary: Use the Evaluate tab to measure your agent's performance across a batch of test questions or conversations before you publish it.

topics.title: Evaluate an agent (preview)
topics.summary: The Evaluate tab in the new agent experience provides structured, repeatable testing for your agent. Use evaluations to measure agent quality across test cases, track improvements over time, and validate your agent's behavior before you publish it.

topics.title: Run an evaluation for an agent (preview)
topics.summary: After you create a test set with conversations, run an evaluation to measure your agent's performance. The evaluation processes each conversation and produces scored results based on the selected test method.

topics.title: View evaluation results for an agent (preview)
topics.summary: After you run an evaluation, review the results to see how well your agent performed across conversations. The results show quality scores and let you open individual conversations to see the agent's responses.

topics.title: Monitor agent performance overview (Microsoft Copilot)
topics.summary: The Monitor tab gives makers an in-context view of an agent's production health. Use it to understand usage, outcomes, user feedback, reliability, and Copilot credit consumption so you can identify trends and decide where to improve the agent.

topics.title: Monitor an agent (Customer Conversation) (preview)
topics.summary: The Monitor tab for agents powered by the Customer Conversation harness gives you visibility into your agent's performance and activity after deployment. Use it to track conversation sessions, review effectiveness and usage analytics, and understand how users interact with your agent.

topics.title: Use the activity trace to debug your agent (Microsoft Copilot)
topics.summary: The activity trace in agents powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness in Microsoft Copilot Studio shows you exactly how your agent processes each message. Use it to understand your agent's chain-of-thought reasoning, verify knowledge source attribution, confirm tool execution, and troubleshoot errors.

topics.title: Add triggers to an agent (Microsoft Copilot) (preview)
topics.summary: Use triggers to create autonomous agents powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness. Autonomous agents run when an event occurs in a connected service. For example, an agent can respond when an item is created in SharePoint, an email arrives, or a scheduled time occurs.

topics.title: Connected agents overview (Microsoft Copilot)
topics.summary: Connected agents are agents your primary agent can invoke during a conversation. When a user's request falls within a connected agent’s domain, the orchestration runtime can route the request to that agent. This approach lets you build modular solutions where each agent handles a specific domain or task.

topics.title: Model availability and controls (Microsoft Copilot)
topics.summary: The harness used to build this agent uses usage-based billing. Using, building, testing, and evaluating agents might consume Copilot Credits. Learn more in Overview of usage-based billing.

topics.title: Start building
topics.summary: When you open Microsoft Copilot Studio, you can choose from several things to build. This article explains what each option is and where to find documentation to get started.

topics.title: Configure agent details and instructions (Microsoft Copilot)
topics.summary: In the agent details and instructions, define the agent and its behavior. This definition shapes the agent's tone, scope, and response style.

topics.title: Configure agent details and instructions (Customer Conversation) (preview)
topics.summary: In the agent details and instructions, define the agent and its behavior. This definition shapes the agent's tone, scope, and response style, and helps the orchestrator route conversations correctly across a multi-agent orchestration.

topics.title: Monitor and analyze agent performance (Microsoft Copilot)
topics.summary: The Monitor tab shows the production health of your agent. Use it to review outcomes and trends, understand user feedback, inspect sessions and runs, and track Copilot credit consumption.

topics.title: Select a model for an agent (Microsoft Copilot)
topics.summary: The model your agent uses affects its reasoning capabilities, response quality, and performance. You can select and change your agent's model from the Build tab in the components panel.

topics.title: Select a model for an agent (Customer Conversation) (preview)
topics.summary: The model your agent uses affects its reasoning capabilities, response quality, and performance. You can select and change your agent's model from the Build tab.

topics.title: Share agents with other users and makers (Microsoft Copilot)

topics.title: Export and import an agent (Customer Conversation) (preview)
topics.summary: You can export and import an agent powered by the Customer Conversation harness using solutions, so you can move the agent across environments.

topics.title: Test your agent (Microsoft Copilot)
topics.summary: Use the Preview tab in agents powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness in Microsoft Copilot Studio to interactively test your agent before you publish it. Interactive testing lets you verify your agent's responses, check knowledge source accuracy, and confirm that tools and skills work correctly.

topics.title: Overview of usage-based billing
topics.summary: Agents, workflows, and apps powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness and customer conversations handled by Microsoft Contact Center Intelligence use a usage-based billing structure. This article describes how Copilot Credits are measured for these experiences.

topics.title: Understand estimated credit usage
topics.summary: To help you understand the impact of your agent design choices while you build and test, Copilot Studio provides estimated Copilot Credit usage in near real time across the Preview , Evaluate , and Monitor experiences. topics.title: Create a new agent (Microsoft Copilot)
topics.summary: The harness used to build this agent uses usage-based billing. Using, building, testing, and evaluating agents might consume Copilot Credits. Learn more in Overview of usage-based billing.

topics.title: Create an agent (Customer Conversation) (preview)
topics.summary: Create an agent to design multi-agent orchestrations for customer-facing scenarios, such as contact centers and help desks. topics.title: About agents powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness
topics.summary: The Microsoft Copilot harness is a redesigned authoring and runtime environment for building AI agents. It introduces a natural-language-first approach to agent creation, a unified single-surface design, and an enhanced orchestration model that improves response quality and reasoning capability.

topics.title: Connect to Microsoft Copilot Studio with MCP
topics.summary: Microsoft Copilot Studio MCP brings Copilot Studio tools into Model Context Protocol (MCP)-compatible CLIs, developer tools, and agentic interfaces. topics.title: Configure access to Copilot Studio MCP
topics.summary: Configure access so your Model Context Protocol (MCP)-compatible client can launch the Copilot Studio MCP npm package and connect to the service. Installing or registering the server in a client doesn't grant permissions to an environment or authorize every action.

topics.title: Connect to Copilot Studio MCP with Visual Studio Code and GitHub Copilot CLI
topics.summary: Add Copilot Studio MCP to Visual Studio Code or GitHub Copilot CLI by using the Microsoft-published npm package. Your client launches the server with npx and communicates with it over stdio. Sign in and select an environment to access the connected service's tools.

topics.title: Files the agent creates (Microsoft Copilot) (preview)
topics.summary: An agent can create files during a conversation - for example, a report, a spreadsheet, an image, or a code snippet - as the outcome of the work the user requested. The agent surfaces each of these files back to the user so they can review or download it.

topics.title: Set up a shared autonomous agent (Microsoft Copilot) (preview)
topics.summary: When someone shares an autonomous agent with you, or you activate an agent for yourself, use the agent management page to connect required services with your own credentials, configure the trigger settings that the agent owner allows, and turn triggers on or off. topics.title: Configure events (Customer Conversation) (preview)
topics.summary: Use the steps in this article to turn an event on or off, or to edit what happens when an event runs. For a list of available events and what each one does, see Events overview (Customer Conversation).

topics.title: Events overview (Customer Conversation) (preview)
topics.summary: Agents powered by the Customer Conversation harness include an Events section in the Build tab, which opens a Conversation events list. topics.title: Connect to Foundry IQ from an agent (Microsoft Copilot)
topics.summary: Foundry IQ connects your agent to a knowledge base built in Azure AI Foundry. A Foundry IQ knowledge base bundles one or more enterprise data sources together with retrieval and relevance settings into a single, reusable asset. When you connect to a knowledge base that someone in your organization already built and tu…

topics.title: Connect to Foundry IQ (Customer Conversation) (preview)
topics.summary: Foundry IQ is a managed knowledge layer that gives your agent permission-aware, cited answers from your data across Azure, SharePoint, OneLake, and the web. For agents powered by the Customer Conversation harness, you connect to Foundry IQ from the Microsoft IQ section of the Build tab.

topics.title: Hooks (Microsoft Copilot) (preview)
topics.summary: A hook runs one of your workflows automatically when something happens in your agent, such as a session starting, a tool running, or an error occurring. Use hooks when you need something to happen every time, rather than only when the agent decides it's relevant.

topics.title: Add knowledge to an agent (Customer Conversation) (preview)
topics.summary: Knowledge sources define what your agent can access and reference when responding to users. You add and manage knowledge from the Build tab.

topics.title: Add knowledge sources to an agent (Microsoft Copilot)
topics.summary: In the new agent experience, knowledge sources define what your agent can access and reference when responding to users. Add and manage knowledge from the Build tab.

topics.title: Knowledge overview for agents (Microsoft Copilot)
topics.summary: Knowledge sources ground your agent in real data, enabling it to answer questions using your organization's content rather than relying solely on its general training. You configure knowledge from the Build tab.

topics.title: Manage knowledge sources in an agent (Microsoft Copilot)
topics.summary: After you add knowledge sources to your agent, you can view, update, and remove them from the Knowledge tab. Regular maintenance ensures your agent has access to current, relevant content.

topics.title: Available knowledge sources for agents (Microsoft Copilot)
topics.summary: The new agent experience supports several types of knowledge sources. Each type connects your agent to different kinds of content and data.

topics.title: Available knowledge sources for agents (Customer Conversation) (preview)
topics.summary: Agents powered by the Customer Conversation harness support several types of knowledge sources. Each type connects your agent to different kinds of content and data.

topics.title: Manage connected agents (Customer Conversation) (preview)
topics.summary: After you add a connected agent, you can review its details, update its name and description, or remove it from your primary agent.

topics.title: Memory (Microsoft Copilot) (preview)

Agents powered by the Customer Conversation harness have a separate, structured Memory capability with its own retention period and configuration. For that harness, see Memory (Customer Conversation).

topics.title: Memory (Customer Conversation) (preview)
topics.summary: Memory lets an agent powered by the Customer Conversation harness carry approved context from earlier conversations into the next one, so a returning customer is met with continuity instead of a cold start. The agent can recognize open intents, recall what was discussed, and pick up where the last conversation ended.

topics.title: About agents powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness
topics.summary: The Microsoft Copilot harness is a redesigned authoring and runtime environment for building AI agents. topics.title: Agents powered by the Customer Conversation harness overview (preview)
topics.summary: Use the Customer Conversation harness when your agent needs to answer questions and resolve issues for your customers over voice and chat. An agent built on this harness is called a Customer Assist Agent .

topics.title: Manage preview conversations (Microsoft Copilot)
topics.summary: The Preview tab in agents powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness in Microsoft Copilot Studio maintains a history of your test conversations. Use conversation history to review past interactions and track patterns in your agent's behavior over time.

topics.title: Preview and test an agent (Microsoft Copilot)
topics.summary: The Preview tab in agents powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness in Microsoft Copilot Studio provides an interactive testing environment where you can chat with your agent, debug its behavior, and review conversation history, all before you publish.

topics.title: Preview and test an agent (Customer Conversation) (preview)
topics.summary: An agent that looks correct in the Build tab can still fail in conversation. Instructions are guidance, not guarantees: the model interprets them, and the gap between what you wrote and what the agent does only shows up when you actually talk to it. Use the Preview tab to test your agent across both web chat and voice…

topics.title: Connect clients to your agent with the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Agent2Agent (A2A) channels (Microsoft Copilot) (preview)
topics.summary: The MCP client and A2A client channels are available only in early release cycle environments. If you don't see these channels in the Add a channel dialog, your environment isn't part of the rollout yet.

topics.title: Available channels for agents (Microsoft Copilot)
topics.summary: After you publish your agent, you can distribute it through different channels based on where your users already work. Microsoft Copilot Studio supports channels across Microsoft experiences, messaging platforms, websites and apps, contact center platforms, and other communication surfaces.

topics.title: Available channels (Customer Conversation) (preview)
topics.summary: After you publish your agent, you can distribute it through different channels based on where your users already work. You can deploy agents powered by the Customer Conversation harness across multiple channels, from standalone channels like a demo website, web chat, and Teams Phone, to contact centers like Dynamics 3…

topics.title: Deploy an agent (Customer Conversation) (preview)
topics.summary: When you publish an agent powered by the Customer Conversation harness, Copilot Studio creates a prebuilt demo website automatically. Use the demo website to test your agent internally, then deploy it to a live website or Teams Phone when it's ready for customers.

topics.title: Deploy overview (Customer Conversation) (preview)
topics.summary: Agents powered by the Customer Conversation harness in Microsoft Copilot Studio use the Deploy page to move your agent from development into channels that other users can access.

topics.title: Publish overview for agents (Microsoft Copilot)
topics.summary: Agents powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness in Microsoft Copilot Studio use publishing to move your agent from development into a live version that other users can access. Until you publish, your agent is only available in the preview pane.

topics.title: Publish an agent (Microsoft Copilot)
topics.summary: If your organization has blocked a channel due to data policies or due to the type of authentication configuration, you won't be able to select it. Learn more in How data policies affect publishing.

topics.title: Configure advanced settings (Customer Conversation) (preview)
topics.summary: The Advanced tab in the Shared Settings panel groups several lower-level configuration areas.

topics.title: Configure component collections (Customer Conversation) (preview)
topics.summary: The Component collections tab in the Shared Settings panel lists reusable component packages that multiple agents in the orchestration can use.

topics.title: Configure connections (Customer Conversation) (preview)
topics.summary: The Connections tab in the Shared Settings panel lists connector bindings used across the orchestration.

topics.title: Configure agent details and security (Customer Conversation) (preview)
topics.summary: The Details and Security tabs in the Shared Settings panel apply across every agent in the orchestration.

topics.title: Configure entities (Customer Conversation) (preview)
topics.summary: The Entities tab in the Shared Settings panel lists entities shared across every agent in the orchestration, split into Custom and Prebuilt entities.

topics.title: Configure language settings (Customer Conversation) (preview)
topics.summary: The Language tab in the Shared Settings panel controls the languages your agent can respond in, across every agent in the orchestration.

topics.title: Configure settings for agents powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness
topics.summary: The settings for agents powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness in Microsoft Copilot Studio let you configure how your agent behaves, processes content, and authenticates users. The Settings page organizes settings into categories.

topics.title: Settings overview (Customer Conversation) (preview)
topics.summary: Agents powered by the Customer Conversation harness are part of a larger orchestration that can include multiple agents, such as connected agents and sub-agents. topics.title: Configure Topics settings (Customer Conversation) (preview)
topics.summary: The Topics settings tab in the Shared Settings panel determines how your agent responds during Topics conversations, using natural language understanding (NLU).

topics.title: Configure variables (Customer Conversation) (preview)
topics.summary: The Variables tab in the Shared Settings panel lists variables shared across every agent in the orchestration. There are three types of variables:

topics.title: Create a skill for an agent (Customer Conversation) (preview)
topics.summary: You can create custom skills for your agent from the Build tab. Skills define reusable capabilities that the agent can activate when a user's request matches the skill's purpose. Agents powered by the Customer Conversation harness support two types of skills: Generative and Topic .

topics.title: Skills overview for agents (Microsoft Copilot)
topics.summary: Agent skills are portable packages of instructions, scripts, and resources that give agents specialized capabilities and domain expertise. Unlike tools, which connect to external services, skills are self-contained sets of instructions and logic that you can create, share, and reuse across agents. Skills follow an ope…

topics.title: Configure voice settings (Customer Conversation) (preview)
topics.summary: Every agent you create with the Customer Conversation harness supports Speech conversations by default, and Voice is a configurable feature of that Speech modality. Use the steps in this article to adjust voice-specific settings for your agent.

topics.title: Speech and chat settings overview (Customer Conversation) (preview)
topics.summary: Every agent you create with the Customer Conversation harness supports both Speech and Chat conversations by default. You don't choose a channel modality when you create the agent. Instead, you configure how the agent should behave for each modality within the same agent. Voice is a configurable feature of the Speech…

topics.title: Add a sub-agent (preview)
topics.summary: Use sub-agents to let your primary agent delegate a focused intent, such as billing or technical support, to a specialist agent that's built directly inside the same orchestration.

topics.title: Sub-agents overview (Customer Conversation) (preview)
topics.summary: A sub-agent is a specialist agent that you build directly inside your primary agent to handle a focused intent, such as billing or technical support. Unlike a connected agent, a sub-agent shares its configuration, deployment, and application lifecycle management (ALM) with the primary agent it belongs to.

topics.title: Access standard harness agents and agent flows
topics.summary: Copilot Studio supports both the standard harness and the Microsoft Copilot harness. This article explains when you might switch harnesses, what changes when you do, and how to move between harnesses based on your authoring goals.

topics.title: Use task agents (Microsoft Copilot)
topics.summary: A task agent is a helper that your agent uses to complete a focused assignment. The agent that delegates the assignment is called the parent agent. topics.title: Add a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server to your agent as a tool (Microsoft Copilot) (preview)
topics.summary: Model Context Protocol (MCP) is a standard for exposing tools to an agent. When you add an MCP server to your agent, the agent can use every tool that the server exposes during a conversation.

topics.title: Add a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server to your agent as a tool (Customer Conversation) (preview)
topics.summary: Model Context Protocol (MCP) is a standard for exposing tools to an agent. When you add an MCP server to your agent, every tool the server exposes becomes available for the agent to invoke during a conversation.

topics.title: Add a workflow to your agent as a tool (Microsoft Copilot) (preview)
topics.summary: Workflows are automated flows built in Copilot Studio's flow designer. They let your agent execute multi-step processes, such as approval flows, data transformations, and complex business logic. Use workflows for repeated, deterministic processes that your agent can run on demand.

topics.title: Available tools for agents (Microsoft Copilot)

topics.title: Available tools for agents (Customer Conversation) (preview)
topics.summary: Agents powered by the Customer Conversation harness support several types of tools that you can add to your agent. Each tool type connects your agent to different kinds of external capabilities and data sources.

topics.title: Manage and delete tools in an agent (Microsoft Copilot)
topics.summary: After you add tools to your agent, you can manage them from the Build tab. You can view tool details, update the configuration, and remove tools you no longer need.

topics.title: Manage and delete tools in an agent (Customer Conversation) (preview)
topics.summary: After you add tools to your agent, you can view, edit, and remove them from the Build tab.

topics.title: Tools overview for agents
topics.summary: Tools extend what your agent can do beyond answering questions from knowledge sources. They let your agent call APIs, run automated flows, interact with external services, and retrieve real-time data.

topics.title: Add prebuilt contact center tools (Customer Conversation) (preview)
topics.summary: Use the steps in this article to add and configure the Escalate prebuilt tool and the Biometric Authentication voice capability. For a description of what each does, see Prebuilt contact center tools (Customer Conversation).

topics.summary: As AI agents take on critical roles in business processes, the need for reliable, repeatable testing becomes essential. Agent evaluation lets you generate tests that simulate real-world scenarios for your agent. These tests cover more questions and conversations faster than manual, case-by-case testing. topics.summary: Use Copilot Studio to enhance your agents by connecting them to other agents. Agents can hand off user interactions to each other or respond to autonomous triggers. Scale out your solutions efficiently by using modular agents tailored to specific tasks or data sets.

topics.summary: In Copilot Studio, a topic defines how an agent conversation progresses.

topics.summary: In Copilot Studio, you can easily create agents powered by the standard harness by describing what you want your agent to do, in your own words.

topics.summary: In Copilot Studio, you can extend an agent's capabilities by calling external REST APIs using the HTTP Request node. This call can be helpful when you need to retrieve data from an external system or manipulate data on that system.

topics.title: Select a primary AI model for your agent
topics.summary: In Microsoft Copilot Studio, the primary AI model you select for your agent powers generative orchestration. Choose a model based on how much your agent needs in response speed, output quality, reasoning, and cost.

topics.summary: When you create an agent in Copilot Studio, the agent is created within a Power Platform solution. You can create custom solutions to manage your agents across multiple environments, or for pipeline deployments and other application lifecycle management (ALM) scenarios.

topics.summary: System topics are common topics used in conversations with an agent.

topics.summary: As you design your agent in Copilot Studio, use the test panel to see how the agent leads a customer through the conversation. It's a good way to make sure your topics work and that conversations flow as you expect.

topics.summary: There are many ways you can manage your topics. Copilot Studio includes a topic checker that lets you know if there are errors in your topics. topics.title: Add an event trigger
topics.summary: Event triggers allow your agent to react automatically when an event occurs in other systems. You can then define a specific flow of actions for the agent to take in response, or give your agent instructions for how to determine the best actions to take.

topics.title: Event trigger overview
topics.summary: Use event triggers to make custom agents perform actions or call topics in response to something happening. Unlike topic triggers, which require input from a user, event triggers allow an agent to act autonomously in response to the specified event.

topics.summary: Web and Direct Line channel security controls whether clients must provide a Direct Line secret or token to connect to your Copilot Studio agent. Without secured access, anyone who knows the agent ID can connect through the Demo website and Custom website channels.
